At some point, Voat needs to have a serious discussion. We seem to constantly have the exact same dilemma, with no clear-cut way of solving it. In my opinion, the question boils down to what I put in the title: Who owns a subverse?

Reddit's stance has seemed to be hard-line on subreddits: the moderator owns it. Yes they impose their other rules however they see fit, but they do generally seem to unilaterally support mods doing whatever they please.

I think a lot of us may have left Reddit for that very reason (as well Admin's uneven application of rules). Mods having the power to do as they pleased, even at the expense of the community, was really terrible and resulted in a lot of censoring of contrary ideas.

On Voat, there has seemingly always been this ideal that subverses somehow belong to the community. But even then, it`s only certain subs. At some point it seems to have been decided that default subs are community-owned, and private subs are moderator-owned. Then we have the question of large, brand-name, but private subs enforcing very questionable rules. And the question arises, did the moderator build that community, or is it simply the name that attracts all the subscribers.

We need to come to a consensus on what exactly should define a subverse as community-owned.

We need to come to a consensus on what exactly should define a community, and how can that be protected from abuse ("shills", as everyone seems so fond of saying) .

We really don't want every sub becoming /v/Whatever, otherwise the entire system breaks down.

I'd be very interested to hear other Goats' opinions on this matter. We don't need to all agree, but even just having some rules set in stone by our great and humble admin @Puttitout, would make a huge difference. I would be more comfortable with a rule I didn't agree with than with our current make-it-up-as-we-go approach.

If you really want my opinion, I follow 2 thoughts...

1) The more general a subverse is, the less rules they should have. And...

2) Behavior should not be a rule.

What I mean by #1 is that aside from the global rules, a subverse only needs a rule that outlines the kinds of posts that are to be allowed. For example, if /v/gaming doesn't want to talk about pirated games, make it a rule. If someone wants to start up /v/piratedgaming, they are free to do so. But, to make rules that you must tag your posts or they will get deleted, you must put spoilers on everything or it gets deleted, etc. that's too much.

Ans for #2, there should never be a "please be civil" rule Civility is something that can be regulated by the voting system. Behavior for that matter should be regulated by the votes. Not by rules.

Again, so long as they do not break the global rules, let the community vote on the posts and comments. There are already tools in place to help curb brigading a bit, use them.

I also go to my subs as examples of what I'm talking about. /v/YouAreFamousNow is very specific in its content. While I do not delete posts that shouldn't belong there (so long as I can understand why they were posted) I reply to them and let them know that their post was outside the scope of the subverse. With /v/snowboarding I have 1 rule, post must be about snowboarding. That's it. If you want to post a rant about how snowboarders are all stoners and assholes, go ahead. But, don't be surprised when you get downvoated.
